why: An alias names a context, not a text (design doc §10), so it resolves through the current-version pointer. Before the bump the alias resolves to v1; after it, to v2 -- and the v1 decision logged in between still names v1. This is the 'does an alias survive a version bump' question the corpus README asks, answered: it survives, and it moves.
